reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Rarest form of GM2 gangliosidosis, caused by biallelic GM2A variants abolishing the GM2 activator protein rather than the hexosaminidase enzyme itself
The activator is an essential cofactor that presents GM2 ganglioside to hexosaminidase A; without it, degradation fails despite normal enzyme activity
Clinically mimics infantile Tay-Sachs disease with early developmental arrest, hypotonia, progressive neurodegeneration and an exaggerated startle response
A cherry-red spot at the macula is a characteristic ophthalmological finding
Standard hexosaminidase A and B enzyme assays are normal, so the diagnosis is missed unless the activator defect is specifically considered
Diagnosis relies on molecular testing of GM2A or specialised substrate/activator functional studies rather than routine enzyme assays
No disease-modifying therapy exists; care is supportive with a multidisciplinary neurodegenerative approach
reference.pathophysiology: The GM2 activator protein is a small lysosomal lipid-transfer cofactor that extracts GM2 ganglioside from the membrane and presents it to beta-hexosaminidase A for hydrolysis. In the AB variant the activator is deficient while hexosaminidase activity measured against artificial substrates is normal, so GM2 ganglioside cannot be catabolised and accumulates progressively within neuronal lysosomes. Neuronal storage drives the relentless central nervous system degeneration that clinically resembles the other GM2 gangliosidoses.
additionalDifferentials: Sandhoff disease (hexosaminidase A and B deficiency, HEXB)
Other infantile neurodegenerative lysosomal storage disorders
Other causes of a macular cherry-red spot (e.g. sialidosis, Niemann-Pick)
additionalInvestigations: Hexosaminidase A and B enzyme assay (characteristically normal, excluding classic Tay-Sachs and Sandhoff)
GM2A molecular genetic testing to confirm activator deficiency
Ophthalmological examination for a macular cherry-red spot
Brain MRI to characterise the neurodegenerative process
Specialised functional studies of GM2 degradation using natural substrate
Developmental and neurophysiological assessment to document progression
redFlags: Progressive loss of acquired developmental milestones in infancy
Exaggerated startle response with a cherry-red macular spot
Feeding difficulty, aspiration and respiratory compromise as disease advances
reference.prognosis: The infantile presentation is progressive and fatal in early childhood, mirroring classic Tay-Sachs disease; management is palliative and supportive as no curative treatment is available.
pitfalls: Excluding GM2 gangliosidosis on the basis of normal hexosaminidase assays
Overlooking the activator defect as a cause of a cherry-red spot with neurodegeneration
Delaying molecular testing when enzyme results are unexpectedly normal
Not offering genetic counselling and carrier testing to the family
references: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
management: Provide palliative and supportive care as no curative or disease-modifying therapy exists
Manage feeding difficulties and aspiration risk with thickened feeds and gastrostomy as swallowing fails
Provide comfort-directed management of the exaggerated startle, irritability and troublesome secretions
Coordinate multidisciplinary paediatric neurology, therapy services and palliative care
Offer genetic counselling with molecular carrier and prenatal testing for autosomal recessive GM2A disease, since enzyme-based screening is unreliable
